strings.note: Small heading over the recipe book page's character strip: the one thing this drink does that the others do not. 8 px body face, one line, ~296 units.
The undiscounted sheet price, printed small beside the real one when the page's character has moved it. {price} is a dollar figure like $13. 8 px, one short line.
Small caption over the chip that says how the drink is worked (shaken, stirred, built). 8 px, one word.
Small caption over the chip naming the serving glass. 8 px, one or two words.
Small caption over the chip showing how hard the drink is to make. 8 px, one or two words.

Small label starting the recipe book page's line of how the drink is usually dressed — the ice, the twist, the sugared rim that this page is nearly always asked for. Two or three words in capitals, 8 px, on one line with the garnish names after it.

The scale under the recipe book page's five-dot legend: what share of the glass each dot stands for. Keep the five figures and the per-cent sign your language uses; the spacing is what lines them up under the dots, so keep the run about this wide. 8 px, one line, ~296 units.
Name of the lever a drink's character pulls: how long the customer will sit. Shown in capitals beside a 16 px mark. 8 px, one or two words.
Name of the lever a drink's character pulls: whether they order again, and how long they hold the stool. 8 px, one or two words.
Name of the lever a drink's character pulls: what the rest of the bar feels when it goes past. 8 px, one or two words.
Name of the lever a drink's character pulls: the mess it leaves behind to be wiped. 8 px, one or two words.
Name of the lever a drink's character pulls: how forgiving the proportions are. 8 px, one or two words.
Name of the lever a drink's character pulls: what it pays. 8 px, one or two words.
Name of a cocktail's character, printed in the heavy face on the recipe book page. Two or three words at most; it is a bartender's phrase, not a stat.
